content.title: About
content.content: Beef empanada is a traditional Spanish‑Latin American pastry made from a thin dough shell filled with seasoned ground beef, onions, spices, and sometimes vegetables. The pastry is fried until golden, giving it a crisp exterior and a juicy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Empanadas originated in medieval Spain and spread throughout Latin America, where each region created its own filling variations.
The dough is traditionally made from wheat flour, butter, and water, resulting in a light, flaky texture.
Beef fillings are often seasoned with paprika, cumin, and oregano, providing a distinctive aroma.
Empanadas are commonly served as appetizers at festivals, fairs, and sporting events.
In some countries they are baked instead of fried to reduce fat content.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Ground beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Empanadas contain B12, B6, and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Moderate carbohydrates
items.content: The dough supplies energy without causing a rapid blood‑sugar spike when consumed in reasonable portions.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Fried empanadas can contain a significant amount of saturated fat, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The filling is often salty; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based dough contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Empanadas are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve empanadas hot, either as a standalone snack or with dipping sauces such as salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. They are convenient for picnics, travel, or game‑day gatherings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag; reheat in the oven or microwave until the crust is crisp before serving.
